It is the only live source for identity, lifecycle, acquisition status, access limits, revisions and local verification. changes.note: SpokenNativQA registered as a spoken-QA secondary carrier. Verified before fetching: ungated, public, licence cc-by-nc-sa-4.0 declared on the card, and the official file list totals 364,209,997 bytes over 3,323 files, matching the survey's ~364 MB estimate exactly. Landed complete with byte closure: 3,323/3,323 files, 0 missing, 0 size mismatches, and all 3,311 LFS-backed files verified by SHA-256. The share-alike term is recorded as a claim limit because it attaches to redistributed derivatives. Acquisition note for future waves: the hf-mirror.com mirror does not serve this repository at all (repeated 'Local entry not found' against the pinned revision), so the official endpoint plus the aria2c-based hfd downloader is the working channel.

A scoped AudioBench speech bundle registered as one record with four member configs (common_voice_15_en_test, dream_tts_mcq_test, openhermes_instruction_test, alpaca_audio_test), 22 files and 3,524,177,488 bytes, every config landing with byte closure and zero LFS SHA-256 failures. The important finding is legal, not technical: the AudioLLMs repackagings declare NO licence of their own in either cardData or README, carrying only citations, so upstream terms govern and were made the selection criterion. Configs whose upstream terms are clear were taken; cn_college_listen_mcq_test and public_sg_speech_qa_test are HELD pending an owner licence ruling (exam-recording provenance and IMDA's separate terms respectively), and TED-LIUM 3 configs are held because its no-derivatives term conflicts with derived feature extraction. Sound/music and AudioSet- or FreeSound-derived configs were hard-excluded by the research boundary, paralinguistic configs excluded as outside 'speech and its linguistic content', and configs already governed at original-source identity excluded as duplicates. The full disposition is on the entry's scope_note.

The three larger SAEA-half carriers all landed and are now registered as their own entries. SD-QA: 22,266 recording references resolve against 22,037 unique English wav with 0 missing, 22,064 payload files and 3,289,716,933 bytes over 11 dialects and both splits, 28.621 audio hours, 0 genuine header failures. SpokenWOZ: byte closure on all three acquired subsets (18 files, 2,481,729,692 bytes, 0 missing, 0 LFS SHA-256 failures); train-split audio deliberately skipped because the study is training-free. WearVox: the mono half closed at its full 3,842 files and 4,499,678,584 bytes with the three root metadata files present; the 54.894 GB multichannel half is deferred by design. Two general lessons for future waves are recorded on the entries: hf-mirror.com serves neither SpokenNativQA nor WearVox, and a raw-HTTP file-by-file fetch must be driven from a list pruned to the not-yet-present files, because aria2c otherwise burns the whole window re-checking files it already holds.

The verification facts established BEFORE fetching each of the three, retained because they are the audit trail for the verify-then-fetch rule. SD-QA: official source is github.com/ffaisal93/SD-QA under Apache-2.0 (the WillHeld/SD-QA Hugging Face mirror declares no licence and was therefore not used); the English subset is 11 dialects (aus, gbr, ind_n, ind_s, irl, kenya, nga, nzl, phl, usa, zaf) across dev and test, with constant questions per dialect. Both git paths failed here — a blob-filtered partial clone stalled with a dead fetch, and the ghfast.top proxy returned HTTP 504 on the 6.4 GB pack — so the working channel is per-file raw.githubusercontent fetches at a pinned commit, driven by the audio_file column of each dialect metadata.csv (22,037 English wav). SpokenWOZ: licence CC BY-NC 4.0 per the official spokenwoz.github.io project page, which designates four Hugging Face repositories as the distribution point; those repositories themselves declare no licence, so the project page is the licence of record. Total 12,823,386,187 bytes over 4 repositories, free and ungated, no form. WearVox: ungated, public, cc-by-nc-4.0, 59,449,535,253 bytes over 7,688 files. Its payload splits into wav/ (3,842 mono files, 4.500 GB) and wav_mc/ (3,842 multichannel files, 54.894 GB) over the same recordings, so the mono half is fetched first as the part a mono-consuming frozen core can actually use. Measured official-endpoint throughput on large files is 3.16 MB/s, projecting roughly 5.2 hours for the full repository; the mirror serves nothing for this repository.

The Mandarin subsets remain unextracted and are out of scope for this English-only study.

Recording, not changing, a SLURP storage redundancy found during this wave. The same audio payload is reachable at both datasets/slurp and repos/slurp/scripts/audio as distinct files rather than links, and both source archives (slurp_real.tar.gz 3,918,185,662 bytes and slurp_synth.tar.gz 2,839,670,545 bytes) are retained alongside their extracted contents. Measured apparent size is 26G under datasets/slurp and 13G under repos/slurp. Note that DrvFS synthesises inode numbers, so the link-versus-copy determination rests on the du figures rather than on inode identity. asset_catalog.transcript_quality_evidence: STRONGEST human-verbatim guarantee of any meeting corpus held by this program, and it is human-ORIGINATED rather than machine-then-corrected. The paper states verbatim that the transcription process 'for the development and evaluation sets relies on close-talk recordings and is conducted entirely without human access to machine-generated transcriptions', explicitly to avoid the machine bias whereby 'competing algorithms will be penalized for deviating from the transcription algorithm'. On segmentation and adjudication it states: 'attendees wore close-talk microphones ... Human annotators then corrected any segmentation errors, and additional throat microphones were employed for quality control. For most meetings, transcription was carried out independently by two professional transcribers, with a third judge resolving non-consensus cases.' The conclusion restates that 'Annotations were created based on the agreement of multiple human listeners'. Local byte-level corroboration: disfluencies and backchannels are retained at a 4.01 percent share of dev1 tokens (um 424, uh 651, hmm 844, mm 720), and the transcripts carry a full verbatim markup scheme for self-truncation, fillers, laughter, backchannels and unintelligible speech rather than cleaned-up prose.

asset_catalog.claim_limit: CC BY 4.0 requires attribution on any downstream use or release. TWO SUBSTANTIVE LIMITS ON WHY THIS CORPUS WAS QUEUED. (1) ENTITY DENSITY DOES NOT HOLD. This corpus was admitted to the queue on the hypothesis that it combines entity density with human-verified verbatim transcripts; the verbatim half is confirmed and exceptionally strong, but the entity half is refuted. The meetings are scripted generic-scenario discussions ('Design the car of the future', 'Electric scooters regulation', 'Holiday gifts for the staff'), participants are pseudonymous aliases, person-name spans are wrapped in <PName> tags, and there is no entity annotation layer at all. Measured capitalised-token candidates run 14-16 per 1000 words but are dominated by segment-initial function words; genuine named entities are sparse and common-knowledge (Europe 34, Mars 16, Tuesday 37, Mexico 30, ChatGPT 13, Airbnb 9), with no rare domain-specific entities of the kind that make Earnings21/22 and ConEC useful for entity-biasing work. Do NOT cite NOTSOFAR-1 as an entity-dense carrier; cite it as a verbatim, speaker-attributed, far-field meeting carrier. (2) SPEAKER OVERLAP IN DEV1. The upstream README warns that dev1 has 12 speakers, 10 of which also appear in the training set; the evaluation sets are disjoint from training in both speakers and rooms, so eval_full is the sound choice for any held-out claim.
